column1: # SURFACES WORTH WATCHING -- the list is DECLARED here, the verdict is DERIVED.
# docrender/tokenaudit.py reads this file, searches every stylesheet WE ship for
# each `probe`, and prints how many of our rules mention it. Zero means Material
# paints that surface and no theme token can change it.
# WHY A HAND-WRITTEN LIST AT ALL, given this repo has killed several. Because the
# alternative needs a manifest of every class MkDocs Material ships, which we do
# not have and would have to maintain -- a bigger hand-written list to avoid a
# smaller one. The split that makes this safe: a human says what is worth
# WATCHING, the build says what is TRUE. The day somebody adds a rule for
# admonitions, that row flips to governed on its own with no edit here.
# ⭐ THAT PROMISE CAME DUE ON 2026-08-05 AND IT HELD. theme/blocks.tsv now
# governs all twelve admonition families, and the three admonition rows below
# flipped from NOT OURS to a rule count without anybody touching the verdict
# column. Only the NOTES needed rewriting, because they described a state of the
# world rather than a thing to watch.
# A row going stale therefore costs a row nobody needed, never a wrong answer.
# ADDING ONE is a row. `probe` is a plain substring matched against our selector
# text, so keep it specific enough not to collide: `.md-typeset` would match
# almost everything and prove nothing.
# surface   what a reader sees
# probe     substring searched in OUR selectors
# note      why it matters, and what it would take to govern it
surface
Admonition / callout blocks
column3: GOVERNED as of 2026-08-05. The border, the title bar wash, the icon colour and the collapsible marker all come from theme/blocks.tsv via blocks.css, and the box structure (width, radius, size, shadow) from the forms and typography vectors. STILL MATERIAL'S: the icon GEOMETRY and the SVG itself, reachable through --md-admonition-icon--<name> but only by authoring image data, which does not belong in a colour table.

column1: Admonition title bar
column3: GOVERNED. The 10% wash is color-mix over the family token, computed in the browser because Material computes its own at Sass time from a literal. The icon inside it is a mask whose COLOUR we set and whose SHAPE we do not.

column1: Collapsible blocks
column3: GOVERNED. Every rule blocks.css emits is written for both spellings -- .admonition.<name> and details.<name>, .admonition-title and summary -- because the rule making Material treat them alike lives in a file that pass did not read. A selector matching nothing costs bytes; a missing one costs a family that stays blue.

column1: Tabbed content
column3: Tab labels, the active underline and the panel border. Material's, and the active colour follows its accent rather than ours. The likeliest next candidate: the structure is simpler than an admonition and the vocabulary is ours to name.

column1: Search panel
column3: The overlay, the input, the result list and the term highlight.

column1: Footnotes
column3: The rule above them, the backref arrow and the numbering.

column1: Code block chrome
column3: Syntax colours come from a Pygments stylesheet, not from our tokens. Our --dr-code-bg only sets the surface behind it, so a theme change repaints the box and not the code. Governing this means generating a Pygments theme from the palette, which is a real piece of work rather than a rule.

column1: Copy-to-clipboard button
Keyboard keys
column3: The raised key styling on ++ctrl+c++. NOTE its box-shadow reads --md-shadow-z1, which base.css now maps to elev-1 -- so the elevation is ours and the colours are not.

column1: Task list checkboxes
column3: The tick, the box and its accent colour.

column1: Table of contents
column3: The right-hand contents rail and its active marker. Distinct from the primary nav, which we DO govern.

column1: Blockquote
column3: The left rule and indent on a plain markdown quote. ⚠️ Not the same thing as the `quote` ADMONITION, which is governed -- a reader typing `>` and a reader typing `!!! quote` currently get different treatments.

column1: Horizontal rule
column3: Material draws its own colour and weight.

column1: Anchor permalink
column3: The paragraph mark beside a heading on hover.

column1: Announcement bar
column3: Not in use today; listed so a future one is not mistaken for a themed surface.
